### N-1: Nghi Son 2 TPP (Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 2)

**Existence/status confidence: MEDIUM**

Nghi Son 2 is a 1,200 MWe (2 × 600 MW) supercritical coal-fired BOT project located in Nghi Son Economic Zone, Thanh Hoa Province. The project is developed by a consortium comprising Marubeni Corporation and Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), with financing from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) and insurance from Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI). The project was structured as a 25-year BOT agreement with EVN as the offtaker.

Unit 1 achieved commercial operation in late 2021 and Unit 2 in 2022, though exact COD dates vary across secondary sources. The project was notable as one of the largest Japanese-financed coal power investments in Southeast Asia and attracted scrutiny from environmental groups regarding coal lock-in. JBIC's involvement is documented in JBIC project lists (URL not verified). GEM's Global Coal Plant Tracker (2023) records both units as operating. Capacity is recorded as supercritical per project technical documentation; gross/net distinction not specified in available sources.

**Conflict note:** Some sources cite total capacity as 1,200 MW, others as 2 × 600 MW net; the 2 × 600 MW figure is used here as it is consistent with the BOT agreement structure.

### N-2: Vung Ang 2 TPP (Nhiệt điện Vũng Áng 2)

**Existence/status confidence: LOW**

Vung Ang 2 is a 1,200 MWe (2 × 600 MW) supercritical coal BOT project in Ha Tinh Province. The developer consortium originally comprised Mitsubishi Corporation, J-Power (Electric Power Development Co.), and Vietnam Steel Corporation (Tổng Công ty Thép Việt Nam). ### N-8: Thai Binh 2 TPP (Nhiệt điện Thái Bình 2)

**Existence/status confidence: MEDIUM**

Thai Binh 2 is a 1,200 MWe (2 × 600 MW) supercritical coal plant in Thai Binh Province, developed by PVN/PVPOWER. The project was originally scheduled for COD in 2014–2015 but became one of Vietnam's most delayed and politically sensitive power projects.

The delays were caused by: (1) EPC management failures by PVN's subsidiary PVC (Petrovietnam Construction Corporation); (2) a major anti-corruption investigation that resulted in the prosecution and imprisonment of senior PVN and PVC officials, including former PVN chairman Nguyen Xuan Son; (3) financing gaps and cost overruns. The project was eventually restructured and construction resumed under new management. Unit 1 achieved commercial operation approximately in 2023 and Unit 2 in 2024, based on PVN press releases. The project is historically important as a case study in Vietnam's anti-corruption campaign (Đốt lò — "Stoking the furnace") intersecting with energy infrastructure.
